newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols stay firm as spot slides.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols stay firm as spot slides.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options stayed firm in thin pre-holiday U.S. trading as the spot dollar tumbled out of recent ranges, sliding beneath 1.54 marks, dealers said.
They said both the spot and option markets had become very choppy because of low volume and the scarcity of price makers.

"There seemed to be some dollar-call selling (in dollar/mark), probably on profit-taking," said Masao Okada, chief options dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank in New York. "And a resultant delta-hedge dollar selling (by market-makers) in the thin market probably helped the dollar go down."
The foreign exchange market was to be closed virtually around the world on Wednesday due to the New Year's Day holiday, and most U.S. traders were likely to go home early today.
A Canadian bank trader said the market was very thin, making price quotes elusive.
"There's really nothing out there," she said.
One-month dollar/mark implied volatilities rose nearly half a point from late Monday levels to about 8.9/9.1 percent in early afternoon U.S.

Traders said a big move in spot dollar/mark had been overdue, especially given the recent breakout in dollar/yen, after month-long consolidative trading that resulted in a clearly visible triangle formation on the daily chart.
They noted that implied volatilities began creeping up on Monday, before the spot dollar started sliding from the 1.5550-1.5600 mark range of the past several days.
Dollar/yen implied volatilities were mostly steady as the dollar drifted around 116.00 yen.
One-month dollar/yen volatility stood at 9.0/9.2 percent, virtually unchanged from late Monday.
Okada at DKB noted that while bidding was not aggressive, volatilities were underpinned by willingness of many traders to buy on dips.
Risk-reversals, which reflect pricing differential of puts and calls, stayed bid for yen puts in shorter-dated dollar/yen as Japanese exporters, the perennial buyers of yen calls, kept a low profile.
One-month 25-delta risk-reversal stood at 0.1/0.4 percent skewed for yen puts. Yen calls were still marginally favored in the three-month area and clearly bid six-months and out.
Traders said dollar/yen risk reversals had been persistently skewed toward yen calls this year, and any flip at the front end did not last for more than a few sessions.
"Risk-reversals could be telling us the dollar's upmove is over, but a lot of things in the market have changed since mid-year and you just never know," Okada said.
